questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere far away from home, which was english speaking and had a good academic reputation in an interesting city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, i think as long as you read the emails on your UCLA mail, then there won't be any issues.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any special assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, you need to apply through UCLA housing, then you just have to make a prioritised list of living arrangements and that's it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I stayed at Tipuana which was a very nice place. I had a friend who made a lot of friends in his apartment, but i didn't in the same way since they were very busy. Although it might look expensive at around 1200-1300 USD/month it is not significantly more expensive than finding something yourself and in this way you can have confirmed housing and no chance of being scammed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just came and checked in with the housing place (i guess only if you get the UCLA housing) and then as far as i remember there was a small intro meeting for exchange students you had to go to, and then you also had to check in at another location on campus, none of it was complicated at all.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get emails about most of the stuff, and if in doubt you can just write them and they are very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be on top of your UCLA email, and if you want to take a graduate course reach out to the professor, they are usually very friendly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was significantly easier than at UCPH but it was also more practical so that was nice. If you are going on exchange purely to get an academic challenge i wouldn't recommend UCLA (i study mathematical economics at UCPH), but if you want to explore LA and California then it is a good compromise.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: One thing you have to keep in mind is that they have a lot of homework which counts towards your grade, so that was a bit different to UCPH. It is more comparable to danish high school than University especially for the undergraduate courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ECON 144, ECON 160, ECON 186, STATS 205, STATS 147, ECON 130, ECON 187, MGMT 126.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ECON 144 was a pretty nice course where you learn about a lot of different forecasting method, it is not as detailed as you would expect coming from UCPH, but it is nice to get an overview of available models. Note that this course has a LOT of homework and projects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think there were any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think everything is just a bit more expensive in LA. I expected eating out and fastfood would be cheaper than at home but in my experience it isn't really.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you arrive in the winter quarter, you have missed the main application time to a lot of the clubs so therefore you shouldn't expect to be allowed in any of the more popular clubs. If there is something specific you want i would recommend at least reaching out a while before you arrive.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sporting events which were very nice, especially the Basketball games where tickets are only $17 for students. Again if you arrive in the winter quarter you can't expect to be able to watch the football team which by the way plays around 2,5-3 hours of public transport from the school (i think there might be a bus for the games, but those would still take around 2 hours.) that being said i definitely would have gone if there was a game during my stay.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the sporting games, those are very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try some different dining spots in LA. I also went to a lot of sporting events and i can especially recommend hockey (LA Kings) and basketball (LA Lakers), just keep in mind that Lakers tickets are usually around $100 minimum and Kings are around $30-50

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, not really

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing specifically

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very polite, i.e. holding the door for each other and stuff like that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You need grants, otherwise it will be very expensive. Go in the spring and winter quarters, another argument for this is that i had to postpone a UCPH exam because of my stay at UCLA, which i now have to take after my stay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing people back home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
